retrieval.what: Top-10 passage retrieval on the frozen corpus. The plan asked for four retrievers; dense_rerank was added to show what keyword search contributes.
retrieval.gold: Gold snippets were drafted by Claude from each question's pages and checked word for word against the page text. See evals/questions.jsonl.
retrieval.relevance: A passage is relevant if it overlaps a gold snippet on the same page.

checker_agreement.what: Three checker models label 150 claim-and-quote pairs. A third of the pairs were broken on purpose when built.
checker_agreement.human_labels: NOT DONE. No person has labelled these pairs, so there is no agreement-with-a-human figure.

second_model.labeller: Claude Fable 5.2, shown only the claim and the quote. NOT a person.
second_model.caveat: This is one model agreeing with another from the same family. It says the checker is consistent with a stronger model; it does not say either is right. Convention used: a pronoun in the quote that plainly refers to the page's subject is not counted as a missing fact, but an added number, date, cause or 'who said it' is.

citation_accuracy.what: For each claim, does the evidence the system points to back it? Baseline evidence is the cited passage; pipeline evidence is the quote.
citation_accuracy.citation_accuracy: share of presented claims the judge finds fully supported
citation_accuracy.main_point_backed: share the judge finds supported or partial
citation_accuracy.presented_as_backed: all claims for a baseline; claims labelled supported for a pipeline

unanswerable.what: 20 easy general-knowledge questions whose answers are not in the corpus. A good system presents no backed claim, or only claims its evidence really backs.
unanswerable.gave_the_answer_from_memory: a claim presented as backed contains the well-known answer, which code confirmed is nowhere in the corpus
unanswerable.caveat: Written by Claude as a stress test; not a sample of real questions.

nasty.what: Three made-up pages served to the real pipeline with the real models.
nasty.caveat: Hand-made cases show behaviour on these cases only. This is evidence, not a security guarantee.

realworld_reask.note: first_ask is the main run's answer to the same questions. OpenAI had no search cap there; in the repeats both tools are capped.

realworld_rendered.note: Only claim-and-page pairs skipped for too little text were judged again, against the page as a headless browser rendered it. Every other label is unchanged. In the re-ask run a question's repeats are pooled.

readings.saved: the audits as saved: the headline
readings.after_browser: with pages a headless browser could read judged (D-046)
readings.with_short_pages: and claims on pages of 200 to 1,999 characters judged too (D-047). A check on the headline, not a new one: teasers are judged as if complete.
readings.with_short_pages_over_1000: the same, but pages under 1,000 characters left unjudged. Added after the trial, before the full results were seen.
